title: Koszul regularity is independent of the smooth ambient scheme
statement: Let $S,T,P,P\prime$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with morphisms $P\to S$ and $P\prime\to S$ smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $i:T\to P$ and $i\prime:T\to P\prime$ be immersions over $S$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. An immersion is called Koszul-regular if locally at each source point it is a closed immersion into an open subscheme of its target, with ideal locally generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]; the empty sequence is allowed. For every $t\in T$, the immersion $i$ is Koszul-regular on an open neighbourhood of $t$ if and only if $i\prime$ is Koszul-regular on an open neighbourhood of $t$. No Noetherian, flatness, separation, or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Fix $t\in T$ and suppose $i$ is Koszul-regular on an open neighbourhood $U$ of $t$. Restrict both maps to $U$. These are still immersions: for an immersion $T\hookrightarrow O\hookrightarrow P$ with the first arrow closed and $O$ open, remove the closed subset $i(T\setminus U)$ from $O$; the restriction $U\to O\setminus i(T\setminus U)$ is a closed immersion, followed by an open inclusion in $P$. The same argument applies to $i\prime$. The Koszul-regularity on $U$ is exactly the assumed local condition; no assertion of regularity on all of $T$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 069E, opening neighbourhood restriction; immersion factorization as in schemes.tex Tag 01IO.

proof.text: Form $Q=P\times_S P\prime$ with projections $p:Q\to P$ and $q:Q\to P\prime$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Both projections are smooth. Here is the base-change argument explicitly: for any smooth $X\to S$ and any $Y\to S$, the projection $X\times_S Y\to Y$ is locally of finite presentation by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. For an affine first-order thickening $D\subset D_1$ over $Y$ and a $Y$-map $D\to X\times_S Y$, formal smoothness in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] lifts its $X$-component to an $S$-map $D_1\to X$. Pair the lift with the given $D_1\to Y$ using the fibre-product universal property. Its restriction to $D$ is the original map since both components agree. Thus the projection is formally smooth, hence smooth. Apply this with $(X,Y)=(P\prime,P)$ and $(P,P\prime)$; the universal property identifies the first product with $Q$ by exchanging the factors.

source.place: Tag 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), using the infinitesimal definition Tag 02H0; local finite presentation base change Tag 01TS.

proof.text: The maps over $S$ give $j=(i|_U,i\prime|_U):U\to Q$ with $pj=i|_U$ and $qj=i\prime|_U$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Apply [lem-zl-immersion-cancellation] to $U\xrightarrow{j}Q\xrightarrow{p}P$: the composite $i|_U$ is an immersion by step 1, so $j$ is an immersion. This checks the immersion hypothesis needed by both comparison lemmas without assuming either ambient scheme separated over $S$.

source.place: Tag 069E, product map j; morphisms.tex Tag 07RK (lemma-immersion-permanence), part (1).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-koszul-immersion-smooth-lift] to $U\xrightarrow{j}Q\xrightarrow{p}P$, with its composite $i|_U$. The projection $p$ is smooth by step 2, both maps from $U$ are immersions by steps 1 and 3, and $i|_U$ is Koszul-regular by the choice of $U$. Thus $j$ is Koszul-regular.

source.place: Tag 067S (lemma-lift-regular-immersion-to-smooth), Koszul-regular case; application in Tag 069E.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-koszul-immersion-smooth-push] to $U\xrightarrow{j}Q\xrightarrow{q}P\prime$, with composite $i\prime|_U$. Now $q$ is smooth by step 2, the two maps from $U$ are immersions, and $j$ is Koszul-regular by step 4. Hence $i\prime|_U$ is Koszul-regular. This proves the forward implication on a neighbourhood of $t$. For the reverse implication start with a neighbourhood on which $i\prime$ is Koszul-regular and repeat steps 1--4 with $P,i$ and $P\prime,i\prime$ interchanged, then this same push lemma with projection to $P$. All hypotheses are symmetric, so it gives Koszul-regularity of $i$ on that neighbourhood.

source.place: Tag 0693 (lemma-push-regular-immersion-thru-smooth), Koszul-regular case; symmetric argument of Tag 069E.

proof_origin.place: Tag 069E (lemma-koszul-independence-factorization), with the product-immersion and smooth-base-change hypotheses checked explicitly.
